About the Scholarship

LAHP has no new studentship funding for 2026/27 or later. This record is retained as historical information; check participating universities for alternative arts and humanities funding.

OpportunityFully Funded PhD Studentship: LAHP AHRC Studentships (London Arts & Humanities Partnership)
HostKing's College London
LocationLondon, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded, stipend provided, tuition covered
StipendUKRI-rate stipend + Research/training support
Application DeadlineNo new LAHP funding for 2026/27 or later; check the participating university for alternatives.
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding Round Discontinued

The London Arts and Humanities Partnership states that its final funded cohort began in autumn 2025 and that no new funding is available for 2026/27 or later. The previously listed January 2027 deadline is not a confirmed application round.

Funding status (verified October 2026): LAHP has confirmed that its final funded cohort began in autumn 2025 and that no new LAHP studentship funding is available for 2026/27 or later. This page is retained for reference only - do not apply to LAHP for 2027 entry. AHRC-funded alternatives in London include other doctoral training partnerships and the open competition route; check the AHRC studentship finder and individual department funding pages for current rounds.

Check the participating university for alternative funding. This retained record is not an invitation to submit a new LAHP application.

Official LAHP funding notice

What LAHP Funded

LAHP (London Arts & Humanities Partnership) was an AHRC doctoral training partnership led by King’s College London with a consortium of London universities. Studentships followed the standard AHRC package: the UKRI minimum stipend (£20,780 for the 2025/26 year of the final cohort) with home tuition fees paid, plus research training and cohort activities across the partner institutions. With no new AHRC funding allocated from 2026/27, applicants to London humanities PhDs should instead target other DTPs, CDA schemes and departmental studentships, or the AHRC open competition where their university participates.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/funding/arts-humanities-research-council-studentships

Source: kcl.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Closed - no new LAHP funding for 2026/27 or later - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About King's College London

King's College London is a public research university and a Russell Group member. Its undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes span medicine, law, humanities, psychology, science and other disciplines. With campuses across central London, King's connects academic study and research with healthcare institutions, cultural organisations and wider questions affecting contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: No new LAHP funding for 2026/27 or later; check the participating university for alternatives.. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
